desc: The book that made Roswell a case. Charles Berlitz and William L. Moore built it on Stanton Friedman's February 1978 contact with Maj. Jesse Marcel Sr. and on the second-hand Barney Barnett material relayed by Vern Maltais, and its publication by Grosset & Dunlap in 1980 converted a thirty-three-year-old retracted press release into an active investigation that would eventually pull in a New Mexico congressman, the General Accounting Office, the Office of the Secretary of the Air Force and two official reports. Two features of the 1980 text are load-bearing for everything that followed. First, it introduced the two-site structure - debris on the Foster ranch, an intact craft elsewhere - by importing the San Agustin material, and that structural decision is the origin of the multi-crash constructions that later Roswell books could never reconcile. Second, it explicitly describes Walter Haut, the officer who wrote the 1947 press release, as 'not a witness' - a baseline against which Haut's subsequent 1989, 1993 and 2002 statements can be measured, and the reason his escalation is documentable rather than merely asserted. Moore's later admission that he had been cooperating with Air Force counterintelligence from around 1980 casts a provenance shadow over the whole publication window.
